chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him)

Regarding the hermaphrodite who has both what is for males and what is for females, he (peace be upon him) said: 'It inherits from the place from which it urinates. If it urinates from the male part, it inherits the inheritance of the male, and if it urinates from the place of the female, it inherits the inheritance of the female.'

And regarding the hermaphrodite who has neither what is for men nor what is for women, except for a hole from which urine comes out, upon which inheritance would it inherit? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If, when it urinates, it projects its urine (to a distance), it inherits the inheritance of the male, and if it does not project its urine, it inherits the inheritance of the female.'
ai.seo_question: How is the inheritance of a hermaphrodite determined in Shia fiqh based on urination?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'takhayyur' (choice) in inheritance for hermaphrodites, relying on the physical evidence of urination to determine gender identity. It highlights the Shia juristic method of using observable biological functions to resolve ambiguity in legal status, ensuring equitable distribution of estate shares based on the most probable gender classification.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>)

regarding the birth of a child for it was what is there for the males and what is for the women. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would inherit from the place which it urinates from. If it urinates from the male part, it would inherit the inheritance of the males, and if it urinates from the place of the women, it would inherit the inheritance of the women’.

And about the child born, there was neither for it what is for the men, nor was there for it what is for the women, except for a hole from which the urine comes out. Upon which inheritance would it inherit?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it urinates to a distance it would inherit the inheritance of the males, and if it did not urinate to a distance with his urine, it would inherit the inheritance of the women’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from certain persons of our people who have narrated the following: “About the case of a newborn who has the reproductive organs of both male and female, one of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘Such person inherits according to the case of the organ from which the urine comes. If he urinates from the male organ he inherits the share of a male person; if she urinates from the female organ she inherits the share of a female/

This is about a newborn who does not have an organ like male or female. However, has only a hole. One of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said that such person inherits like a male; if it (urine) comes with a dart but if it does not reach far away then that person inherits like a female/”
